chapter_summary.title: Motion in a Plane — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This chapter introduces 2D kinematics through vectors, projectile motion and uniform circular motion. The key idea: 2D motion under constant acceleration splits into two independent 1D problems linked only by time.

sections.heading: Projectile motion
bullets: A projectile moves under gravity alone (air resistance neglected).
Horizontal velocity is constant; vertical acceleration is g downward.
Range R = u² sin 2θ / g; maximised at θ = 45°.

sections.heading: Uniform circular motion
bullets: Speed is constant; velocity direction changes continuously.
Centripetal acceleration a_c = v²/r toward the centre.
Centripetal force F = mv²/r is the NET inward force — not a new kind of force.

sections.heading: Relative velocity
bullets: v_AB = v_A − v_B — a vector subtraction.
River-crossing: shortest time = head straight across.
Shortest path = head upstream so the cross-current component cancels.

key_takeaways: Resolve every 2D vector problem into perpendicular 1D components.
Projectile: parabolic trajectory; T, H, R all from u and θ.
Uniform circular motion is accelerated motion (direction changes).
Relative velocity in 2D is a vector subtraction.

glossary.definition: A body moving under gravity alone after being thrown.
Acceleration toward the centre of a circle: a_c = v²/r.
Horizontal distance from launch to landing: R = u² sin 2θ / g on level ground.

questions.question: On level ground, the range of a projectile is maximum at a launch angle of
questions.explanation: R = u² sin 2θ / g; sin 2θ is maximum at 2θ = 90°.

questions.question: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30°. Find T, H, R. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Apply T = 2u sin θ / g, H = u² sin²θ / 2g, R = u² sin 2θ / g.

questions.question: Derive expressions for the time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range of a projectile.
questions.answer: Take launch as origin, x horizontal, y up. u_x = u cos θ, u_y = u sin θ. a_x = 0, a_y = −g. Then x(t) = u cos θ · t and y(t) = u sin θ · t − ½ g t². Setting y = 0 gives T = 2u sin θ / g. At apex v_y = 0 ⇒ H = u²sin²θ / (2g). R = u_x × T = u² sin 2θ / g.

questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 2 m at constant speed 4 m/s. Its centripetal acceleration is
In uniform circular motion, the speed is constant but the velocity changes.
questions.explanation: Speed is the magnitude of velocity; direction of velocity changes continuously even though magnitude is fixed.

questions.question: The range of a projectile on level ground is maximum at a launch angle of ____.

Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A car of mass 1000 kg negotiates an unbanked circular curve of radius 50 m at 15 m/s. μ = 0.5. Take g = 10 m/s².

(i) What centripetal force is required?
(ii) What is the maximum friction the road can supply?
(iii) Can the car make the turn safely?
questions.answer: (i) F_c = mv²/r = 1000 × 225 / 50 = 4500 N. (ii) f_max = μmg = 0.5 × 1000 × 10 = 5000 N. (iii) Yes — required (4500 N) < available (5000 N).
questions.explanation: Compare required centripetal force with maximum available friction.
